risks.risk: Camera may not power on or have a functional shutter/sensor
risks.proof: A video clip showing power-on, shutter firing, and a live-view or test image on the LCD

risks.risk: Shutter count could be very high (common issue on older 5D III bodies)
risks.proof: A photo of the shutter count from camera menu or EOSInfo app

risks.risk: Listed accessories (batteries, charger, trigger) may not actually be included
risks.proof: A photo showing all items laid out together with the camera
risks.if_unproven: priced as body-only, accessories not counted

risks.risk: Sensor or mirror box damage, fungus, or missing internal parts not visible from exterior shots
risks.proof: Close-up photo of sensor with body cap/lens removed and mirror up, plus a sample photo taken with the camera
risks.if_unproven: priced as worst-case condition (possible internal fault)

risks.risk: Mismatch between seller's stated brand (Sony) and actual item (Canon) suggests a templated or unreviewed listing
risks.proof: A corrected, consistent listing description from the seller confirming camera details
risks.if_unproven: treated as a red flag but not sufficient alone to call fraud; priced at worst case for a body-only, unverified-working camera

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on and firing the shutter
Photo of the shutter count from the camera menu
Photo of sensor (lens removed, mirror up) for dust/fungus/damage check
Photo of all included accessories (2 batteries, charger, Godox trigger) laid out with the camera
Clarification of the seller's garbled condition statement and correction of the Sony/Canon brand mismatch
response.reason: Photos clearly identify a Canon EOS 5D Mark III body with no lens, no visible accessories, and no proof of working condition, so it is priced at worst case as a body-alone unit; the text's Sony/Canon mismatch and incomplete condition note are flagged as risks but do not block identification since the camera itself is clearly readable in the photos.
